translations.text: The words of Amos, which came in Akkarim from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, king of Judea, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the great earthquake.
And he said: The Lord spoke from Zion, and from Jerusalem he gave forth his voice; and the pastures of the shepherds mourned, and the summit of Carmel dried up.
And the Lord said: For three impieties of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they sawed apart with iron saws the pregnant women in Gilead.
And I will send fire upon the house of Hazael, and it shall devour the foundations of the son of Hader.

And I will break the bars of Damascus, and I will destroy the inhabitants of the plain of On, and I will cut off the tribes from among the men of Canaan; and the chosen people of Syria shall be taken captive, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: For three impieties of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they took captive the captives of Solomon and brought them into Idumea.
And I will send fire upon the walls of Gaza, and it shall devour its foundations.
And I will destroy the inhabitants of Azotus, and I will take away a tribe from Ashkelon, and I will stretch out my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the foreigners shall perish, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: For three impieties of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they brought the captives of Solomon into Idumea and did not remember the covenant of brothers.
And I will send fire upon the walls of Tyre, and it shall devour its foundations.

Thus says the Lord: For three impieties of Idumea, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they pursued their brothers with the sword; and he destroyed the mother upon the earth, and seized her as a testimony and as a terror to him, and he kept his onslaught for victory.
And I will send fire upon Teman, and it shall devour the foundations of its walls.

Thus says the Lord: For three impieties of the sons of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they ripped open the pregnant women of the Gileadites in order to enlarge their own borders.
And I will kindle fire upon the walls of Rabbah, and it shall devour its foundations with shouting in the day of battle, and it shall be shaken in the day of its end.
And its kings shall go into captivity, and their priests and their princes together, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: For three and for four impieties of Moab, I will not turn away from it, because they burned [?] the bones of the king of Idumea to dust.
And I will send fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the foundations of its cities; and Moab shall die in weakness, with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet.
And I will destroy the judge from it, and I will cut off all its princes with him, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: For three impieties of the sons of Judah, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they forsook the law of the Lord and did not keep his commandments; and their vain things which they had made led them astray, which their fathers had followed after them.
And I will send fire upon Judah, and it shall devour the foundations of Jerusalem.
Thus says the Lord: For three impieties of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for sandals.

They trample the dust of the earth, and they beat the heads of the destitute with their fists, and they have turned aside the way of the lowly. Son and father went in to the same maidservant of theirs, so that they might profane the name of their God.
And they stretched out their garments with cords as coverings beside the altar, and in the house of their God they drank wine gained by false accusation.
But I took away the Amorite from before them. His height was like the height of a fir tree, and he was strong like an oak. I took away his fruit above and his root below.
And I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and I led you around in the wilderness for forty years, so that you might inherit the land of the Amorites.
And I took some of your sons to be prophets, and some of your young men to be consecrated. Is this not so, sons of Israel? says the Lord.
But you made the consecrated ones drink wine, and you commanded the prophets, saying to them: "Do not prophesy."
Therefore, behold, I will roll beneath you, as a cart full of reeds rolls.
And the runner will have no way to flee, and the strong man will not hold on to his strength, and the warriors will not save themselves.
And the archer will not stand his ground, and the man swift of foot will not escape, and the horseman will not save himself.
And his heart was found in strength; the naked will pursue him on that day, says the Lord.
Hear the words that the Lord has spoken against you, O house of Israel, and against every tribe that I brought up from the land of Egypt. And I said
that you alone have I known out of all the tribes of the earth; therefore I will take vengeance on you for all your wickedness.
Will two walk together at all unless they know each other?
Will a lion roar from his thicket when he has no prey? Will a lion's cub cry out from his den at all unless he has seized something?
Or will a bird fall to the ground without a fowler? Or will a snare be set on the ground without catching something?
Or if a trumpet sounds in the cities, will the people not tremble? Or if there is evil in a city, has the Lord not done it?
For the Lord God will do nothing unless he reveals his teaching to his servants the prophets.
The lion has roared, and who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, and who will not prophesy?

Proclaim it to the regions in Assyria and to the regions of the land of Egypt, and say to them: "Gather on the mountain of Samaria, and see the many wonders in its midst and the oppression within it."
And it did not know what would come before it, says the Lord: they are the ones who store up falsehood and misery in their regions.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: O Tyre, your land round about will be laid waste, and your strength will be brought down from you, and your regions will be plundered.

Thus says the Lord: As a shepherd snatches two [?] (legs?) or the base of an ear out of a lion's mouth, so the sons of Israel who live in Samaria before the tribes, and in Damascus, the priests, will be snatched away.
Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, says the Lord God Almighty.
For on the day when I take vengeance on Israel for his ungodliness, I will also take vengeance on the altars of Bethel. The horns of the altar will be broken off and will fall to the ground.
I will smash the house with wings all around, together with the summer house. The houses of ivory will perish, and many other houses will be added to them, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: Hear these words, you heifers of Bashan who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor and trample on the fallen, who say to your lords, "Give us wine, so that we may drink."

The Lord, the Lord, swears by his holy ones: Behold, days are coming upon you when I will carry you off with weapons, and they will cast those who are with you into evils, to be kindled from beneath [?].
They will lead you in naked, one in front of another, and you will be cast out to the mountain of Rimmon, says the Lord.
For you went into Bethel and committed lawlessness, and at Gilgal you multiplied ungodliness. In the morning you brought your sacrifices, and on the third day your tithes.
They read the law outside and proclaimed confession. Announce that the sons of Israel have loved these things, says the Lord God.
And I gave you dullness of teeth in all your cities and lack of bread in all your places, yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

And I withheld the rain from you three months before the harvest. I will send rain on one city, and on another city I will not send rain. One portion will be rained on [?], and the portion on which I do not send rain will dry up.
Two and three will gather into one city to drink water, and they will not be satisfied, yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

I struck you with burning heat and with blight. You multiplied your gardens and your vineyards, but the worm devoured your fig groves and your olive groves, and even so you did not return to me, says the Lord.

I sent death among you by the way of Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword, and your horses I gave over to captivity. I made your camp go up in fire in your wrath, and even so you did not return to me, says the Lord.
I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like firebrands snatched out of the fire, and even so you did not return to me, says the Lord.
Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel. But because I will do this to you, prepare to call on your God, Israel.

For behold, I will make the thunder strong and create the wind, and I will declare his anointed one to men. I made the dawn and the mist, and I will walk upon the heights of the earth. The Lord God Almighty is his name.
Hear this word of the Lord, a lament that I bring upon you, O house of Israel.
She has fallen. The virgin daughter of Israel will never rise again. She has sinned in her land, and there is no one who will raise her up.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: The city from which thousands went out will have only hundreds left, and the city from which hundreds went out will have tens left, for the house of Israel.
For thus says the Lord to the house of Israel: Seek me out, and you will live.
Do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, and do not cross over to the Well of the Oath. For Gilgal will surely be carried off into captivity, and Bethel will become as though it had never been.
Seek the Lord and live, so that the house of Joseph does not blaze up like fire and devour it, with no one to put it out for the house of Israel.
He who executes judgment on high, and established righteousness on the earth.

He who makes all things and transforms them, who turns the shadow of death into morning and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth: the Lord is his name.
He who deals out ruin upon the strong, and brings misery upon the fortress.
They hated the one who rebukes in the gates, and they loathed the holy word.

Therefore, because they oppressed the poor, and you took choice gifts from them: you built houses of hewn stone, but you will not live in them; you planted pleasant vineyards, but you will not drink wine from them.
For I know your many impieties, and your sins are mighty. You trample the righteous, take bribes, and turn the poor away from the gates.
Therefore whoever understands will keep silent at that time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live; and so the Lord God Almighty will be with you, as you have said.
"We have hated evil and loved good." So restore justice in the gates, so that the Lord God Almighty may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore thus says the Lord God Almighty: In all the streets there will be lamentation, and in all the roads people will say, "Woe, woe!" They will call the farmer to mourning and lamentation, and those who know how to wail to wailing.
And there will be lamentation in all the roads, for I will pass through your midst, says the Lord.
Woe to those who long for the day of the Lord! Why do you want this day of the Lord? It is darkness and not light.
It is as when a man flees from a lion, and a bear meets him; and he runs into the house and leans his hands against the wall, and a snake bites him.
Is not the day of the Lord darkness? There is no light in it; it is gloom, and it has no brightness.
I have hated and rejected your feasts, and I will not smell the offerings at your assemblies.
Even if you bring me whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not accept them, and I will not look upon the display of your offerings of salvation.
Take away from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the psalms of your hymns.
Let judgment pour forth like water, and righteousness like a river that cannot be crossed.
Did you offer me slaughtered victims and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the images that you made for yourselves.
And I will deport you beyond Damascus, says the Lord; God Almighty is his name.
Woe to those who despise Zion, and to those who trust in the mountain of Samaria! They harvested the first of the nations, and they themselves went in, O house of Israel.
Cross over, all of you, and see. Go from there to Hamath and to Rabbah, and go down to Gath of the Philistines, the strongest of those kingdoms, and see whether their territory is greater than yours,
you who are coming to an evil day, who draw near and take hold of false sabbaths.
They sleep on beds of ivory and take their pleasure on their couches. They eat kids from the flocks, and calves from among the tender [?] suckling ones.
You clap along to the sound of the harp. They count themselves as abiding, and not as fleeing.
They drink strained wine and anoint themselves with the finest ointment, and they were not grieved at all over the ruin of Joseph.
Therefore they shall now be taken captive at the head of the mighty, and the neighing of horses shall be taken away from Ephraim.

For the Lord, the Lord, has sworn by himself, says the Lord God of hosts: "I abhor all the arrogance of Jacob, and I have come to hate his land. I will take away the city together with those who live in it."
And if ten men are left in one house, they shall die, and the remnant shall be left.

Their kinsmen shall take them up and shall be forced to carry their bones out of the house. He shall say to those in charge of the house, "Is there still anyone with you?" And he shall say, "No more." And he shall say, "Be silent, because of naming the name of the Lord."
For behold, the Lord shall give the command, and he shall strike the great house with breaches and the small house with cracks.
Will horses run in pursuit over rocks? Or will they keep silent toward the mares? For you have turned judgment into wrath, and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness.
You rejoice over a word of nothing, and you say, "Have we not gained horns by our own strength?"
"For behold, I will raise up against you, O house of Israel," said the Lord God of hosts, "and they shall oppress you, so that you shall not enter Hamath, and as far as the torrent of the west."
Thus the Lord God showed me: behold, a brood of locusts coming at dawn, and behold, a locust [?] Gog [?] the king.
And when it had finished devouring the grass of the land, I said, "Lord, Lord, be merciful! Who will raise up Jacob? For he is diminished."
"Relent, O Lord, concerning this." "And this shall not be," says the Lord.
Thus the Lord, the Lord, showed me: behold, the Lord God called for judgment by fire, and it devoured many deeps, and it devoured the portion.
And I said, "Lord, Lord, cease! Now who will raise up Jacob? For he is diminished."
"Relent, O Lord, because of this." "And this shall not be," says the Lord, the Lord.
Thus the Lord showed me: behold, someone standing on walls of adamant, with adamant in his hand.
And the Lord said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "Adamant." And the Lord said, "Behold, I am setting adamant in the midst of the people of Israel. I will no longer pass him by."
"And the altars of laughter shall be destroyed, and the idol-shrines of Israel shall be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."

Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam king of Israel and said to him, "Amos is stirring up a gathering of the people against you in the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words.
For this is what Amos says: 'Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall be led away captive from its own land.'"
And Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go, get away from here! Go off to the land of Judah, and there you may [?], and there you may prophesy.
But you shall no longer prophesy at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary, and it is the king's house."
Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I was not a prophet, nor the son of a prophet. I was a shepherd, and I pruned sycamore figs."
And the Lord took me from following the sheep, and the Lord said to me: Go and prophesy against my people Israel.
And now hear the word of the Lord. You say to me: Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not stir up the people against the house of Jacob.

Therefore thus says the Lord: Your wife shall play the harlot in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be measured out with a line, and you shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall be carried off captive from its land.
Thus the Lord the Lord showed me: and behold, a fowler's vessel. And the Lord said to me: What do you see, Amos? And I said: A fowler's vessel.
And the Lord said to me: The end has come upon my people Israel; I will not pass by them again.
And the ceilings of the temple shall cry out on that day, says the Lord. Many are the fallen in every place, and I will bring silence upon them.
Hear this, you who crush the poor in the morning and oppress the needy of the land,
and who say: When will this month be over, so that we may sell, and the Sabbath, so that we may open the storehouses, to make the measure small, to make the weight large, and to make a false balance,
so that we may buy the needy for silver and the poor for a pair of sandals, and trade in every kind of goods?
The Lord swears by the pride of Jacob: if all your deeds are filled up [?] for ever...
And shall not the earth tremble at these things, and all who dwell on it mourn? And the end shall rise up like a river, and shall sink back like the river of Egypt.
And on that day, says the Lord the Lord, the sun shall go down at noon, and the light shall be darkened on the earth in the daytime.

And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation, and I will put sackcloth on all loins, and baldness on every head. And I will make it like the mourning for a beloved one, and those with him like a day of pain.
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord the Lord, when I will send a famine on the land: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord.
And the waters shall be stirred up as far as the sea, and from the north to the rising of the sun they shall run to and fro, seeking the word of the Lord, and they shall not find it.
On that day the fair virgins and the young men shall faint from thirst,
those who swear by the propitiation of Samaria, and who say, 'As your god lives, O Dan,' and 'As your god lives, O Beersheba.' They shall fall and never rise again.

I saw the Lord standing upon the altar, and he said: Strike upon the altar, and let it be shaken before the gates, and cut it off upon the heads of all of them; and the rest of them I will kill with the sword. No fugitive of theirs shall escape, and none of them who tries to escape shall be saved.
Though they hide in hell, from there my hand shall drag them up; though they climb up to heaven, from there I will bring them down.

If they hide on the top of Carmel, from there I will search them out and bring them back; and if they go down out of my sight into the depth of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it shall bite them.
And if they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and I will kill them; and I will set my eyes on them for evil and not for good.
And the Lord God is the one who touches the earth and shakes it, and all who dwell in it shall mourn. Its end shall rise up like a river, and it shall go down like the river of Egypt.
He builds his ascent into heaven and lays the foundation of his promise upon the earth. He summons the water of the sea and pours it out over the face of the earth. The Lord Almighty is his name.

"Are you not like the sons of the Ethiopians to me, O sons of Israel?" says the Lord. "Did I not bring Israel up out of the land of Egypt, and the foreigners out of Cappadocia, and the Syrians out of the pit?"
"Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the kingdom of the sinners, and I will remove it from the face of the earth. But I will not remove the house of Jacob completely," says the Lord.
"For behold, I will give the command, and I will scatter the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is sifted in a sieve, and not one crushed fragment falls to the ground.
All the sinners of my people shall perish by the sword, those who say, 'It will not come near us, and evil will not come upon us.'
On that day I will raise up the tent of David that has fallen, and I will rebuild its ruins as in the days of old,
so that the rest of humankind may seek God, and all the nations upon whom my name has been called," says the Lord, who has done all these things.

"Behold, the days are coming," says the Lord, "when the threshing shall overtake the grape harvest, and the grapes shall ripen at the time of sowing. The mountains shall drip with sweetness, and all the hills shall be covered with plants.

I will bring back the captives of my people Israel. They shall rebuild the ruined cities and live in them. They shall plant vineyards and drink their wine, and they shall make gardens and eat their fruit.
I will plant them in their own land, and they shall never again be uprooted from their land, which I have given them," says the Lord God Almighty.
